title: A dependency that downloads a prebuilt binary on install is high, not critical
intent: The deliberate loud case, and the one most likely to be argued with. prebuild-install / node-pre-gyp style packages fetch a platform binary during install; a dropper fetching a payload looks identical to a scanner. Both mean every consumer install now makes a network request the previous release did not, which is worth a maintainer reading once — so this blocks approval. It stays a tier below the remote-shell dropper because plain HTTPS download has a benign reading and `critical` has to keep meaning that nothing does.
